title: TDP-43 Promotes Amyloid-Beta Toxicity by Delaying Fibril Maturation via Direct Molecular Interaction.
one_liner_zh: 该文用全原子离散分子动力学模拟研究TDP-43与Abeta肽的直接分子互作及对纤维成熟的动力学影响，虽涉及蛋白-肽互作与MD方法，但对象非TF-DNA体系，且无结合位点预测或界面建模，仅部分可借鉴。
abstract: Amyloid-beta (Abeta) is a peptide that undergoes self-assembly into amyloid fibrils, which compose the hallmark plaques observed in Alzheimer's disease (AD). TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) is a protein with mislocalization and aggregation implicated in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and other neurodegenerative diseases. Recent work suggests that TDP-43 may interact with Abeta, inhibiting the formation of amyloid fibrils and worsening AD pathology, but the molecular details of their interaction remain unknown. Using all-atom discrete molecular dynamics simulations, we systematically investigated the direct molecular interaction between Abeta and TDP-43. We found that Abeta monomers were able to bind near the flexible nuclear localization sequence of the N-terminal domain (NTD) of TDP-43, adopting beta-sheet rich conformations that were promoted by the interaction. Furthermore, Abeta associated with the nucleic acid binding interface of the tandem RNA recognition motifs of TDP-43 via electrostatic interactions. Using the computational peptide array method, we found the strongest C-terminal domain interaction with Abeta to be within the amyloidogenic core region of TDP-43. With experimental evidence suggesting that the NTD is necessary for inhibiting Abeta fibril growth, we also simulated the NTD with an Abeta40 fibril seed. We found that the NTD was able to strongly bind the elongation surface of the fibril seed via extensive hydrogen bonding and could also diffuse along the lateral surface via electrostatic interactions. Our results suggest that TDP-43 binding to the elongation surface, thereby sterically blocking Abeta monomer addition, is responsible for the experimentally observed inhibition of fibril growth. We conclude that TDP-43 may promote Abeta toxicity by stabilizing the oligomeric state and kinetically delaying fibril maturation.
abstract_zh: 淀粉样蛋白-β (Amyloid-beta, Abeta) 是一种通过自组装形成淀粉样纤维的肽段，这些纤维构成了在阿尔茨海默病 (Alzheimer's disease, AD) 中观察到的标志性斑块。TAR DNA结合蛋白43 (TAR DNA-binding protein 43, TDP-43) 是一种在肌萎缩侧索硬化症及其他神经退行性疾病中涉及错误定位和聚集的蛋白质。近期研究表明，TDP-43可能与Abeta相互作用，抑制淀粉样纤维的形成并加重AD病理，但二者相互作用的分子细节仍不清楚。利用全原子离散分子动力学 (discrete molecular dynamics) 模拟，我们系统研究了Abeta与TDP-43之间的直接分子相互作用。我们发现，Abeta单体能够结合到TDP-43 N端结构域 (N-terminal domain, NTD) 的柔性核定位序列附近，并采用由该相互作用促进的富含β-折叠构象。此外，Abeta通过静电相互作用与TDP-43串联RNA识别基序的核酸结合界面相关联。利用计算肽阵列方法，我们发现TDP-43 C端结构域与Abeta的最强相互作用位于其淀粉样生成核心区域。基于实验证据表明NTD对抑制Abeta纤维生长是必需的，我们还模拟了NTD与Abeta40纤维种子。我们发现，NTD能够通过广泛的氢键强烈结合纤维种子的延伸表面，并可通过静电相互作用沿侧表面扩散。我们的结果表明，TDP-43结合到延伸表面，从而通过空间位阻阻断Abeta单体添加，这可能是实验观察到的纤维生长抑制的原因。我们得出结论，TDP-43可能通过稳定寡聚状态并动力学上延迟纤维成熟来促进Abeta毒性。
